1_myfxbook.name: Myfxbook
1_myfxbook.auth_notes: Free Myfxbook account needed. Login returns session ID (IP-bound, 1-month TTL). No paid plan required for basic access.

community_outlook.returns: JSON with forex sentiment for all pairs
community_outlook.value: HIGH - retail positioning data across all major forex pairs

scraping_alternative.notes: Public page shows sentiment for all pairs without login. Can scrape as fallback.

autotrade_systems.scraping_notes: Public page listing strategy providers. API only provides data for YOUR accounts, NOT other traders. Must scrape HTML to get public system data.
autotrade_systems.limitation: No API endpoint for browsing other traders' systems - HTML scraping only

1_myfxbook.python_example:
import requests

# Step 1: Login
login_url = 'https://www.myfxbook.com/api/login.json'
resp = requests.get(login_url, params={'email': EMAIL, 'password': PASSWORD})
session_id = resp.json().get('session')

# Step 2: Get community sentiment
outlook_url = 'https://www.myfxbook.com/api/get-community-outlook.json'
resp = requests.get(outlook_url, params={'session': session_id})
sentiment = resp.json()
# Returns: {symbols: [{name: 'EURUSD', shortPercentage: 45.2, longPercentage: 54.8, ...}]}

2_gains_network_gtrade.name: Gains Network (gTrade) - Forex Positions
2_gains_network_gtrade.auth_notes: Fully public REST API. No API key needed.

trading_variables.returns: All pair definitions including forex pairs with indices
trading_variables.notes: Use this to build pair_index -> symbol map. Forex pairs are in group indices around 32-45.

open_trades_by_address.returns: Array of open trade objects for specific trader

trading_history_24h.returns: All trades from last 24 hours across all traders
trading_history_24h.notes: Use to discover active forex traders by filtering pairIndex 32-45

personal_history.returns: Full trade history for a trader

forex_pair_indices.notes: Full list from /trading-variables. Group type indicated by isForexOpen flag.

2_gains_network_gtrade.forex_filtering_strategy: Fetch /trading-history-24h, filter trades where pairIndex is in [32-45] range. These are the forex traders. Then fetch their full history and open positions.
2_gains_network_gtrade.rate_limit: No documented limit but use 0.5-1s delay between requests. 429 responses possible.
2_gains_network_gtrade.python_example:
import requests

BASE = 'https://backend-arbitrum.gains.trade'
FOREX_PAIRS = range(32, 46)  # Forex pair indices

# Get 24h trades, filter forex
history = requests.get(f'{BASE}/trading-history-24h').json()
forex_trades = [t for t in history if int(t.get('pairIndex', -1)) in FOREX_PAIRS]

# Find active forex traders
from collections import Counter
trader_counts = Counter(t.get('trader', '') for t in forex_trades)
top_forex_traders = trader_counts.most_common(20)

# Get their open positions
for addr, count in top_forex_traders:
    trades = requests.get(f'{BASE}/open-trades/{addr}').json()
    forex_open = [t for t in trades if int(t.get('pairIndex', -1)) in FOREX_PAIRS]
2_gains_network_gtrade.enhancement_needed: Add forex-specific filtering. Current scraper handles all pairs but doesn't filter by asset class.
2_gains_network_gtrade.priority: P0 - Already have scraper. Just add forex pair filter.

3_dailyfx_ig_sentiment.name: DailyFX / IG Client Sentiment
3_dailyfx_ig_sentiment.auth_notes: Web page is public. No documented JSON API.

sentiment_page.notes: Redirects to ig.com. Shows long/short % for major forex pairs, gold, indices.
sentiment_page.data_rendered_via: JavaScript (dynamic content, needs Selenium or browser automation)

individual_pair_pages.notes: Per-pair sentiment pages with detailed positioning data

3_dailyfx_ig_sentiment.scraping_challenge: Content is JavaScript-rendered. Basic requests.get() returns empty data. Need Selenium/Playwright or find underlying XHR endpoint.
3_dailyfx_ig_sentiment.alternative_approach: Use Myfxbook community outlook instead - same type of data, easier to scrape via JSON API.
3_dailyfx_ig_sentiment.python_example:
# DailyFX requires browser automation due to JS rendering
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto('https://www.dailyfx.com/sentiment')
    page.wait_for_selector('.dfx-sentiment-table')  # Wait for data to load
    # Extract sentiment data from rendered HTML
    rows = page.query_selector_all('.dfx-sentiment-row')
    for row in rows:
        pair = row.query_selector('.pair-name').inner_text()
        long_pct = row.query_selector('.long-pct').inner_text()
        short_pct = row.query_selector('.short-pct').inner_text()
3_dailyfx_ig_sentiment.priority: P2 - Use Myfxbook instead. Only pursue if you need IG-specific data.

5_forexfactory_calendar.name: ForexFactory Economic Calendar
5_forexfactory_calendar.auth_notes: Public page but Cloudflare-protected. No official API.

impact_levels.title_attribute: span[title] contains 'High Impact Expected', 'Medium Impact Expected', 'Low Impact Expected', 'Non-Economic'

scraping_challenges: Cloudflare bot protection - basic requests may get 503 Service Unavailable
Need User-Agent header and possibly cookies
Date cells span multiple rows (shared across events on same day)

market-calendar-tool.usage: from market_calendar_tool import scrape_calendar; df = scrape_calendar()
market-calendar-tool.notes: Pre-built scraper that returns pandas DataFrame. May handle Cloudflare.

5_forexfactory_calendar.python_example:
import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

url = 'https://www.forexfactory.com/calendar?day=today'
headers = {
    'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36',
    'Accept': 'text/html,application/xhtml+xml'
}
resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
soup = BeautifulSoup(resp.text, 'lxml')
table = soup.find('table', class_='calendar__table')
rows = table.select('tr.calendar__row.calendar_row') if table else []

events = []
for row in rows:
    currency = row.select_one('td.calendar__currency')
    event = row.select_one('span.calendar__event-title')
    impact_span = row.select_one('td.calendar__impact span')
    actual = row.select_one('td.calendar__actual')
    forecast = row.select_one('td.calendar__forecast')
    previous = row.select_one('td.calendar__previous')
    
    events.append({
        'currency': currency.text.strip() if currency else '',
        'event': event.text.strip() if event else '',
        'impact': impact_span.get('title', '') if impact_span else '',
        'actual': actual.text.strip() if actual else '',
        'forecast': forecast.text.strip() if forecast else '',
        'previous': previous.text.strip() if previous else '',
    })
5_forexfactory_calendar.priority: P1 - Valuable for event-driven forex strategy. Calendar events cause volatility.

8_mql5_signals.name: MQL5 Signal Marketplace (MetaTrader)
8_mql5_signals.auth_notes: Public leaderboard pages. No official API for signal data.

signal_list.notes: JavaScript-rendered page. Basic requests returns incomplete data.

scraping_challenges: Dynamic content - needs Selenium or Playwright
Rate limiting - 403 errors if too many requests per second
8_mql5_signals.python_example:
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
import time

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto('https://www.mql5.com/en/signals/mt5/list?type=forex&sort=gain')
    page.wait_for_selector('.signals-table')
    
    rows = page.query_selector_all('.signals-table tr')
    signals = []
    for row in rows[1:]:  # Skip header
        cells = row.query_selector_all('td')
        if len(cells) >= 6:
            signals.append({
                'name': cells[0].inner_text().strip(),
                'gain': cells[1].inner_text().strip(),
                'subscribers': cells[2].inner_text().strip(),
                'drawdown': cells[3].inner_text().strip(),
                'weeks': cells[4].inner_text().strip(),
            })
8_mql5_signals.priority: P1 - Rich forex strategy performance data. Proven scrapers exist.

10_etoro.name: eToro Discovery API
10_etoro.auth_notes: Discovery/rankings endpoint appears to work without authentication based on OpenAPI spec. No API key documented.

rankings_discovery.returns: JSON array of investor profiles with performance stats
rankings_discovery.notes: Extremely powerful discovery endpoint. Filter by gain, risk, copiers, win rate.

bullaware.auth: API key from bullaware.com/api (free tier available)
bullaware.notes: Covers ~10,000 eToro portfolios. Easier than scraping eToro directly.

10_etoro.python_example:
import requests

# eToro discovery - find profitable forex traders
url = 'https://www.etoro.com/sapi/rankings/rankings/'
params = {
    'period': 'CurrYear',
    'gainmin': 15,
    'riskscore': 4,
    'copiersmin': 50,
    'winratiomin': 55,
    'sort': '-gain',
    'pagesize': 50
}
headers = {'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0'}
resp = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers)
if resp.status_code == 200:
    traders = resp.json()
    for t in traders.get('Items', []):
        print(f"{t.get('UserName')}: Gain={t.get('Gain')}% Risk={t.get('RiskScore')} Copiers={t.get('Copiers')}")
10_etoro.priority: P1 - JSON API, no auth documented, rich filtering. Verify the endpoint still works without auth.

technical_notes.browser_automation: Several sources (FXSSI, MQL5, ZuluTrade, ForexFactory) require Playwright or Selenium for JavaScript-rendered content. Playwright is recommended over Selenium for headless scraping - lighter weight and faster.
technical_notes.playwright_install: pip install playwright && playwright install chromium
technical_notes.rate_limiting: All sources should use 1-3 second delays between requests. Myfxbook has explicit 100 req/day limit on free tier.
technical_notes.user_agent: Always set realistic User-Agent header. Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36
technical_notes.data_normalization: All sentiment data should be normalized to: {pair, long_pct, short_pct, source, timestamp} for cross-source aggregation
